1._: THE SHARED SHAPE — Most people never change a default, so the default is where authority would creep back in. The default arrangement is therefore computed, never authored: the nestings that recur across people's arrangements, drawn as a reading anyone can make again. Arrangements cannot be compared address by address, because my first place is not yours. They are compared by relation: which proposal sits under which.

1.2: WHERE AUTHORITY CREEPS IN — When one person's reading becomes everyone's structure: an arrangement made into a spine that all must fit. That is a reading act stored as a shared write, and it is the one move to refuse.
1.3: WHY A PAGE NEVER BALLOONS — The character sheet grows to swallow the whole game only if containment is written into its content. Kept in arrangements and references, nesting costs a page nothing, and every page stays its own size.
1.4: PHASES WITHOUT A RULE — A proposal that grows can evolve in place, which is a content write, or hand on to a next-phase page, which is a structure write that arrangements then point on to. Two change what everyone reads: a page's content, which is what it says, and the structure — a new page, a nesting, a reference. 1.3: NOT A MIRROR — On the beach a mirror voices a spine's addresses, so it can only reflect that spine's nesting — which brings back the authority. An arrangement is the person's own tree instead, each position pointing at a proposal by reference: one block's point becomes another block's entry, the way the starstone's hidden directories join blocks. That is inclusion without containment.
1.4: THE X-RAY AND THE Y-RAY — The X-ray sees through one body to its bone: the trail, read when something hurts. The Y-ray is the flock as one person sees it: their own arrangement, the form of the murmuration from where they fly. There is no single Y-ray. There are as many as there are people arranging.
1.5: COPYING IS THE COUPLING — A newcomer starts from someone's arrangement, then moves whatever doesn't fit them. What spreads that way is how a murmuration keeps its shape: each bird adjusting to its neighbours, and nobody deciding the flock.
1.8: DECIDE — Is this the shape: each person keeps their own arrangement of the proposals, anyone may look at it and copy it, and none of them is the structure? David, Matthew and James are asked; anyone may answer.
1._: THE Y-RAY — Each person keeps their own arrangement of the proposals: the ones they care about, nested as they see them, tap by tap. Anyone can look at anyone else's and copy it as a start. Nobody's arrangement is the structure, and the proposals themselves stay as their makers keep them. David's would be at happyseaurchin.com/proposals/happyseaurchin, and anyone's at /proposals/ and their name.

1.2: THE PIT STOP AND THE CLASSROOM — A Formula One crew arranges itself round the car. Four wheels, one nut each, all four sides at once in under three seconds, because the car fixes where everyone stands. Learning maths has no car. The structure the teacher has to fit is forming inside the student, which is why learning goes best when the student makes the teacher: Freire's teacher-student and students-teachers, Bakhtin's dialogue. The beach already handles the car kind well — a house, a game, a codebase. The trouble starts when it treats the classroom kind the same way.
1.3: BONE IS LAID DOWN BY LOAD — Bone forms along the stresses it actually carries, and is resorbed where it is not used (Wolff's law). An endoskeleton is not designed and then lived in; it is the deposit of living. On the beach that deposit is the trail: each act standing in the block of the mind that made it, with threads tied from those acts. The trail persists, and it is read from where you stand — where am I, who am I with, what is my next knot.
1.4: THE X-RAY — A picture of the whole is useful the way an X-ray is: taken when something hurts, read, and put away. That gives a test for any page or form. If someone has to write into it in order to act, it is a shell, and it becomes the authority. If it can be thrown away and redrawn from what people have already done, it is an X-ray. The beach's streams already work the second way: each person's line stands in their own mirror, the fold is made by whoever asks for it, and a fold that is kept can be superseded by anyone and is never a gate.
1.5: THE MEMBRANE — Building is chains: glucose chained into cellulose for a plant's cell walls, its cousin chitin for a crab's shell. A membrane has no chains. It holds because each molecule takes its own stance towards the water around it, and nothing bonds one molecule to the next. On the beach the water is the shared clock: everyone says where they are at a time, and nobody writes into anyone else.
1.6: WHAT EACH PERSON NEEDS — Proprioception, not anatomy. Starlings in a murmuration each track six or seven neighbours, never the whole flock (Ballerini and colleagues, 2008). Each person needs their own place, the people they are with, and their next knot. The whole form only now and then.
1.8: DECIDE — Is this the problem: one shared arrangement of the proposals would become a shell we all plug into, when what each of us needs is to know where we are and who we are with? David, Matthew and James are asked; anyone may answer.
1._: SHELL OR BONE — When a structure is the place where we act, it becomes the authority: we plug into it, and it holds us in place. That suits building a thing, where the thing itself decides where everyone stands. It does not suit how we organise ourselves. What holds us there has to be inside, like bone: invisible, felt rather than seen, informing what each of us does without anyone looking at it. One shared arrangement of the proposals would be a shell.
